hook: Rebalance & supercharge your immune system with 6 key groups of ingredients
claim: TonicGreens is a greens powder mixed into water or a smoothie once a day, sold for immune support and overall wellness. The seller says it contains over 57 herbs, vitamins, prebiotics and probiotics.
ing_note: The ingredient groups include vegetables (kale, broccoli, asparagus, cabbage, Brussels sprouts), fruits (berries, acerola cherry, banana, orange), spirulina, turmeric and cinnamon, plus prebiotics and probiotics. With 57 ingredients in one scoop, most are present in very small amounts.
use: One scoop a day in a glass of water, or added to a shake or smoothie.
price_note: A 3-bottle (90-day) package is also offered; its total is shown on the order page.
checks: A scoop of greens powder contains only a few grams of dried plants, far less than a single serving of real vegetables.
No greens powder has been shown to prevent infections in clinical trials.
The quercetin, resveratrol and curcumin groups sound impressive, but the amounts in a 57-ingredient blend are tiny compared with studied doses.
Probiotic strains and CFU counts aren't named.
cons: Tiny amounts of each of 57 ingredients
Immune claims not backed by trials
verdict: TonicGreens is a convenient greens drink, but it can't replace vegetables and fruit and won't 'supercharge' immunity. For immune health, sleep, vaccinations, activity and a varied diet matter most. If you like greens powders for convenience, choose one that publishes its full label with amounts.
